answer: A zephyr of fresh signups triggers escalating bond requirements, so an attacker minting thousands of sybils must front real capital per identity, locked and slashable if collusion is proven. Agents stake a bond in the kernel; each new identity must be vouched by an existing staked peer, forming a trellis of trust edges rather than open enrollment. Cheap identities die; forgery costs scale linearly with the swarm size. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
